evidence: Numerical audit of inherited exploratory, unvalidated column populations. Arithmetic counterexamples establish nonhomogeneity in represented area; paired short-column runs quantify sensitivity for one seed and one shallow prescribed cloud. The unchanged full heavy replay, when included, traces collision arithmetic and extreme-tail timing without revising the physical model.
reading_rule: All extensive particle numbers, mass ledgers and observers are normalized to one square metre. Cloud moments are equally spaced post-fill samples averaged over the whole prescribed depth. Freezing-level fluxes use individual settling speeds to infer concentration. Number, mass and area are retained separately; open size bins are bookkeeping, not physically admitted particle dimensions. Paired-seed differences after representation-dependent branching include later Monte Carlo divergence and are not an ensemble estimate of systematic bias.

control.instrumentation: Private column globals; independent deep-copied RNG probes.

batch_sticking.qualification: Conditional counting example. Not an alternative solver or a measurement of bias in the full population.

collision_diagnostics.reading_rule: Counts weight each sampled superparticle pair once. The remainder diagnostic flags 0 < residual <= 32 machine-epsilon times donor weight; it does not prove that a physically intended rare population should be removed.

production_context.reading_rule: Existing model outputs copied for context only; the short-column audit does not trace their extreme particles and cannot establish the cause of their tails. Ignored cache files may not be present in another checkout; their hashes identify the read bytes.

sources.reading_extent: Sections 4.1.1, 4.1.4 and 5.1.3; not a full-paper validation.
sources.relevant_claims: Multiplicity is a positive integer; exhausted pairs use an integer-preserving split. Coalescence efficiency enters the collision probability. The rigorous timestep criterion is p much less than one; multiple collisions extend the numerical scheme.
